children: Beena Parmar Bengaluru: Five out of the top six Indian technology companies sequentially doubled job additions in the September quarter to 10,300, overcoming concerns that artificial intelligence (AI) would shrink employment in the country's most globally tracked industry through automation and an inevitable revenue squeeze. In the $315-billion industry, with a combined 7.52% weighting on the Nifty as of end-September, Wipro was the only company to shed jobs, reducing its headcount by 6,700. Data showed the top six had added a net 5,500 to their rolls in the April-June quarter. Employee data of Infosys, the country's second-largest software exporter, isn't included in these calculations as the company is due to announce earnings on October 23 and hasn't shared its latest manpower data.
Excluding Wipro's reductions, Tata Consultancy Services (TCS), HCLTech, Tech Mahindra and LTM (formerly LTIMindtree) added a massive 17,100 employees in the second quarter.

title: Software Majors Add More Hands in Q2 on Deal Wins, Growth Optimism
